plan.english: The first man and the twin were brothers. The twin was dear to the man. Together they drove the sheep and the cattle into the field. There they found a strewn place under an oak. There the man built a hearth. He gave the fire libated honey. The gods spoke to him: "Make the first sacrifice." "Seize your brother, the twin." He heard the word of the gods, and his heart trembled. Then he seized the twin and slew him. The twin did not cry out. That was the first sacrifice. The man sat down by the hearth. He did not speak. From the twin's flesh the earth came forth. From his head the sky was made. The earth was flat and broad. The sun stood above. And they gave the man good fame. The twin's name became famous.

title: The World from the Twin's Body

plan.english: The twin lay in the field. The gods came to him. They sat down around him. They slit him open. They cut the flesh from the bones. From it they made the earth. They broke the bones. From them they made stones. The blood ran out. From it they made the waters. They cut off his head. From it they created the sky. From his mind the moon came forth. From his tears came the rain-clouds. They set the sun above. They threw the stars into the night. Then they saw their work. And it was good. They walked on the earth. They drank the waters.

Then the man led the twin to the strewn place. He looked at the strewn place. The sun stood above. He spoke: "I see the fire and the stones." "Where are the sheep? Where are the cattle?" The man said: "You are the sacrifice, brother." Then the twin took fright. He did not flee. He lay down on the strewn place. He looked at the sky. The man slew him. The man's heart trembled. His blood ran out onto the strewn place. The earth drank it. The man stood there. He did not see his brother.

The man sat down at the hearth. He cried out. "Brother, where are you?" Then a voice came from the earth. It spoke. "Brother, do not weep." "I am the earth, and I carry you." "I nourish you." "The sky is my head." "The moon is my mind." "The rain-clouds are my tears." "Drink my waters." "When you die, I cover your bones." "Do not be afraid." The man heard the voice. His heart became glad. Then he stood up.

"Whose flesh is the earth?" "The earth is the twin's flesh." "Whose bones are the stones?" "The stones are his bones." "Whose blood is the sea?" "The sea is his blood." "Whose head is the sky?" "The sky is his head." "Whose mind is the moon?" "The moon is his mind." "Who walks on his flesh?" "Men and sheep walk on it." "Who slew the twin?" "His brother slew the twin." "What was the first sacrifice?" "The twin was the first sacrifice." "What is left of the twin?" "Imperishable fame is left of the twin."

The gods sat down at the hearth. The strewn place lay under the oak. Then the man brought the twin to the fire. They laid him on the strewn place. They gave the fire libated honey. The fire burned and cooked the flesh. They, sitting at the hearth, ate the flesh and drank the blood. The man stood by the fire and looked at the bones. The bones lay in it. It licked the bones. From the bones stones arose. They were joyful. They said to the man: "You made the first sacrifice." Then the gods stood up. Then it dawned.

The first man spoke. "I seized my brother." "I led him into the field." "He did not cry out." "I slew him." "I wept." "From him the earth and the sky were made." "My heart trembles." "Where is my brother?" "That sea yonder is his blood." "This moon is his mind." "Now I walk on it." "I eat, I drink." "Brother, do you hear me?" "May you carry me." The earth carried the man.

Sky saw the slain twin. He cried out. His tears were great. From his tears came the rain-clouds. Then it rained. The earth drank the water. She became full. Then the water swelled in the sea. Blossoms arose. The sheep ate the blossoms. Then the sheep drank the water. When Sky cries out, it rains. Then the earth nourishes the flock with the water. The men plough the field. The men tell this to their sons.

The twin spoke to his brother. "Seize me, brother, and cut me." "May my flesh become the earth." "May my bones become stones." "May my blood become the sea." "May my head become the sky." "May my name be famous." The man heard the twin's word and wept. Then he took a stone. With the stone he cut him. From him the earth and the sky arose. Then the gods set a famous name for the twin. The man went away and looked at the moon.

The gods saw the slain twin. They said to the man: "Man, do not slay your brother." "Give us cattle." "Let them be the sacrifice." Then the man drove them to the fire. He gave the fire libated honey. He said: "Gods, take the cattle." They ate their flesh. They gave him good things. Now men give cattle to the gods. The twin's fame remained. The twin's name is famous.

title: The Sons Part Sky and Earth

plan.english: Sky and Earth lay together. In the night the sons dwelt in between. They trembled. Then the great son rose. He looked at his brothers and spoke: "Let us lift Sky up." "Let us set her down." Standing on the earth, they lifted him up. And they set her down. Then it became bright. They saw the sun and became joyful. Sky stood above, and Earth lay below. Now the great son holds him up. The sun goes between the two. They became gods.

Sky lay on Earth. The men lay under him. They did not stand up. They trembled with fear. A hero had great might. He seized a stone. He struck Sky with the stone. The stone broke. Then the two split apart. He went up, and she lay down. Light came between them. The men stood up. They saw the sun, and they were glad. Then the hero's name became famous. His fame was great. The men tell of the hero's work.

The craftsman stretched the sky above. He laid the earth below. It was flat and broad. Between them he set the mist. He threw the stars into the night. He set the moon above. He yoked swift horses to the wheel of the sun. He made the path of the sun straight. Now the wheel of the sun goes through the sky. The horses draw it. In the night the sun sinks. Then the craftsman looked at his work. It was good. The craftsman sat down. The craftsman's work stands. The men saw the wheel of the sun. They said: "Great is the craftsman's work."

The sons cried out. "Father Sky, go up!" "Mother Earth, lie down below!" "We do not see the sun." "We lie in the night." "We tremble." Sky heard, and he went up. She lay down below. Then it became bright. They saw the light. They became joyful. They cried out again: "Father Sky, giver of good things, stay above!" "Mother Earth, carry us!"

"Where are Sky and Earth?" "Sky is above, and Earth is below." "How did he go up?" "The great son lifted him up." "Whose son was he?" "He was the son of Sky and Earth." "What did the sons see?" "They saw the sun." "Where does the sun go?" "The sun goes in between." "What became of the sons?" "They became gods."

Sky is the father, and Earth is the mother. Sky gives water to Earth. She drinks the water. Then she nourishes the flock and the sheep. The shepherd drives the flock into the field. He milks the sheep. From the sheep the wool grows. The dog guards the sheep. The wolf does not come. They both hear the men. "Father Sky, Mother Earth, give us good things." "Give us water, give us sheep." "Let the sheep be many."

The gods hid the fire from the men. In winter they grew cold. They did not cook the flesh. Then a thief came. Having seized the fire in the gods' hearth, he carried it to the men. The night hid him. The thief was swift. The fire burned in their hearths. They became warm. They became glad. They cooked the flesh and ate it. Then the gods saw the fire in the hearths. They did not speak. The thief's name is famous.

The fire was hidden in the stone. No one knew it. A man sat down by the stone. He struck it with a stone. The fire ran out. He trembled. Then he became joyful. With the fire he cooked the flesh. The night became bright. The men came to it. They sat down around it. They ate the flesh and were sated. Then the man set a name for the fire.

Fire was set in the hearth of the men. He became their guest. He sat in the hearth. He was red. He ate the sacrifice. The men sat at the hearth and looked at him. Fire gave them warmth. He is dear to them. Fire is the master of the dwelling. In the night he is awake. He protects the dwelling. Fire is the giver of good things. Whoever guards Fire, Fire guards him.

title: How the First Man Got Cattle

plan.english: The cattle came forth from the earth. The first man received them. He drove them into the field and milked them. In winter they stood under the oak. They became many. Then the wolf came. The wolf crept toward them. The dog saw the wolf. The dog drove the wolf away. The dog became dear to the man. Since then the dog sits by the hearth. The shepherd guards the cattle. The dog guards the field.

The men had no king. Then a king was set for them. He was the first king. He made the path straight. He shepherded the people. He drove the flock into the field. He gave good things to the people. They heard his words. They became many. His might was great. He had a son. The son became king. His fame was great.

The twin was the first king. He was a shepherd of the people. When he was king, no one died. The sheep did not die. The water did not dry up. Winter did not come. The people were many. Fire burned in their hearths. The sun shone on the field. They did not tremble in the night. Then Death came to the king. He lay down. He died. The people cried out.

A serpent lay in the fort. It seized the cattle. The men trembled. The sheep did not eat. Then a hero came to the fort with swift horses. He slew the serpent. He freed them. He drove them out of the fort. They were glad. The sheep ate. The serpent's bones lay in the field. The men said: "Hero, you slew the serpent." "Your name is famous."

May the cattle stand in the field! May the wolf not come to them! May the snake not seize them! May the thief not drive them away! Dog, guard the sheep! Shepherd, drive the flock into the field! Sky, give water! Earth, nourish the cattle! May the cattle be many! May the king have good fame! May the king's flock be great!

The twin lay down and did not rise. He died. He was the first mortal. No one knew the path. He found it and went along it. The path was long. Then the men followed him. Now he leads the dead along the path. He is the king of the dead. The twin's name is famous. His fame is imperishable.

"Go, dead man, along the path." "Go the way that the twin went." "Follow the twin." "Two dogs guard the path." "Do not be afraid." "Step into the boat." "Do not turn around." "May Sky receive you." "May Earth cover your bones." "May Dawn awaken you." "May your fame be imperishable."

The mother trembled. She sought her son in the field. She cried out his name. "My son, where are you?" No voice came. She saw an old man. "Old man, have you seen him?" The old man answered: "I saw him going along the path." "The twin led him." "Your son is gone." The mother lay down on the earth. She cried out.

The dead go to the water. They leave the earth. They carry no load. There a boat is standing. The boat is light. They sit down in the boat. The boat carries them on the water. The water is flat and broad. On the other side lies a field. Cattle stand there. The twin sits there, and he is king. He sees the dead coming. He gives them seats.

title: The Sun Returns, the Mortal Does Not

plan.english: The sun sinks and comes again. The moon goes and arrives again. Winter goes and arrives again. The mortal goes and does not come again. Death comes to the mortal. The dead do not see the sun. His imperishable fame remains. The famous name does not vanish. Whoever has good fame does not die.

The old man died. His wife cried out. His sons cried out. They carried him to the fire. The fire burned the old man's flesh. The earth received his bones. His name remained. They said: "Father, we remember." "May your name remain famous." Then they gave the fire libated honey. They sat down at the hearth.

A hero saw Death. He said: "Death, where are you going?" Death spoke: "I have come to you." "I seized your father." "Now I am grasping you." The hero said: "Do not seize me!" "Give me imperishable fame." Death said: "I do not give fame, Sky gives it." The hero was silent. Then he went along the path.

When night comes, the mortal lies down. Sleep seizes him. The stars stand in the sky. Dawn awakens him. But no dawn awakens the dead. The dead lie in the earth. The sun becomes bright, but they do not see it. Sleep is the brother of Death.

Father Sky, giver of good things, hear us! You who stand above, you who set the sun up, you who gave the day to us. Dawn, your daughter, comes. The great son lifted you up. Father Sky, give us good fame! Protect us, Father Sky!

Mother Earth, hear us! You who carry the mortals, you who nourish the cattle, you who drink the water of Sky. You are the twin's flesh. Earth, give us sheep and cattle! Mother Earth, may you carry us! When we die, cover our bones.

The wheel of the sun runs through the sky. Swift horses draw it. Dawn dawns, then the sun becomes bright. In the night the sun sinks, and in the day it becomes bright. The sun sees the earth and the sky. May the sun see us, may the sun hear us.

Dawn, daughter of Sky, become bright! You who awaken the mortals, you who bring the light, you who drive the night away. Your light is great. Come to our hearth, Dawn! Awaken us, Dawn, daughter of Sky!

Night comes, and day comes. The moon walks in the night. The sun walks in the day. The stars stand in the sky. Winter comes, and the water grows cold. The sun turns, and winter goes. The snow melts, and blossoms arise in the field. Who set this in order for us? The gods set this in order for us.

Night, come to the mortals! You who cover the earth, you who bring the stars, your stars look at the mortals. The moon walks in the sky. Do not frighten us, Night! May Dawn, daughter of Sky, come to us!

Sky and Earth, hear us! You two are the father and the mother of the gods. Sky and Earth are stretched out. Between you goes the wheel of the sun. Between you it rains, and the cattle drink. You two nourish the mortals and the cattle. Give us good things, you two!

Who stretched the sky? Who laid the earth below? Who set the sun and the moon in the sky? Who yoked the swift horses to the wheel of the sun? Who gave the day to the mortals? The gods know it, and we do not know it. Let us make a sacrifice to them.
